page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD processors. It features a constrained-vCPU design that limits processing cores while preserving the massive memory envelope of the host class, yielding 672.0 GB of total RAM and an elevated memory ratio of 14.0 GB per vCPU.

For temporary and scratch data handling, the instance includes 5669 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The underlying platform supports Premium Storage for remote disk attachments, allowing administrators to combine expansive ephemeral storage with persistent managed disks. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The constrained CPU-to-memory configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads constrained by per-core database software licensing. Organizations running memory-heavy enterprise database engines can reduce licensing overhead while accessing significant RAM and high-capacity local NVMe storage. Workloads that match this profile include large in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, big data analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning software requiring high memory-per-core allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 48 dedicated x86_64 AMD vCPUs on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. It offers an unbalanced compute-to-memory allocation designed for memory-intensive workloads, providing 672.0 GB of RAM at 14.0 GB per vCPU core. In addition to high-capacity system memory, the instance incorporates 5669 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage connectivity. The hardware profile lacks dedicated GPU acceleration. By constraining the core count while retaining a broad memory footprint, the instance optimizes cost efficiency for applications bound by per-core software licensing fees. Recommended workloads include large relational and in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching solutions, and enterprise workloads that require extensive memory density alongside low-latency local scratch space.
